findings.label: Four of five timing workloads are host/launch-cadence bound; kernel time spans 13.9x with no eval-latency movement
findings.backend_detail: msprof op_summary.csv columns 'Task Wait Time(us)' and 'Task Duration(us)' for op _moe_sum_reduce_kernel; 100 measured invocations per workload.

evidence.metric: Task Wait Time(us) per invocation, steady state (rows 97-104 of op_summary)
Task Duration(us) per invocation, steady state
Task Duration(us) / Block Num (512-token case, rows 52-55)
evidence.value: 35.441-35.820 us, Block Num 224, Task Wait Time 77.339-79.459 us

evidence.metric: Task Wait Time(us) on the latency-saturated 4096-token workload (contrast case)

findings.inference: Task Wait Time measures how long a launched task sits queued before the device starts it, so 100-138 us of wait in front of a 2.5-7.4 us kernel is direct evidence that the device is idle waiting on the host, not on the kernel. Because eval latency stays within 91.97-98.11 us while kernel time moves 2.57->35.75 us, these four workloads are pinned to a host-side per-call floor of roughly 92-98 us that is shared in magnitude with the reference implementation (reference latencies 101.15/101.88/96.06 us for the three shapes where its kernel is also tiny). Kernel-side work on these shapes cannot move eval latency until the kernel exceeds that cadence, which only happens at 4096 tokens.

findings.label: 4096-token workload is HBM-streaming but is not at the MTE2 bandwidth roof: 80.4% active with ~1.28 TB/s read rate while active
findings.backend_detail: msprof base collection (100 invocations) plus msprof OpProf kernel-level metrics; aic_* counters are all zero because the kernel runs on AI_VECTOR_CORE only (cube_utilization 0).

evidence.metric: Task Duration(us), Block Num, aiv_vec_ratio, aiv_mte3_ratio
evidence.value: 460.076 us avg (458.309-462.369), Block Num 1792, aiv_vec_ratio 0.4548, aiv_mte3_ratio 0.0604
1) MTE2 bandwidth utilization lower than 80% when active.

evidence.metric: Operator Basic Information: Task Duration(us) / Block Dim (op-profiler run, 10 warmup iters)

findings.inference: Input is 4096x8x7168 bf16 = 469.76 MB and output 4096x7168 bf16 = 58.72 MB (528.48 MB total, all contiguous and each element read exactly once, so logical equals physical volume here). Over the 460.08 us kernel that is ~1.15 TB/s combined and ~1.28 TB/s of read traffic concentrated in the 368.4 us the MTE2 pipeline is active. Since the device is continuously busy on this workload (Task Wait Time ~0) and the vendor op-profiler independently reports MTE2 bandwidth utilization below 80% while active, the remaining ~20% of kernel time is the load pipeline waiting on dependent work rather than a demonstrated bandwidth ceiling. Vector (45.5%) and MTE3 (6.0%) are well below MTE2, so the vector reduce and the output store are not the limiter.

findings.label: 512-token case runs at ~1.85 TB/s effective, 1.6x the HBM-streaming case: L2 residency, so its pipeline ratios are not an HBM proxy
findings.backend_detail: Derived from op_summary durations/ratios and the target L2 size from the service target probe (l2_cache_size=176160768). Residency itself is inference, not a measured L2 hit counter - this level produced no L2 hit-rate metric.

evidence.metric: Task Duration(us) and aiv_mte2_ratio / aiv_vec_ratio (512 tokens, input 58.72 MB)
Task Duration(us) and aiv_mte2_ratio (4096 tokens, input 469.76 MB)

findings.inference: 66.06 MB of traffic in 35.58 us is ~1.85 TB/s, i.e. 1.6x the rate measured on the 470 MB HBM case, while its MTE2 pipeline is active only 37.6% of the kernel. The 512-token working set (58.7 MB) fits inside the 176160768-byte L2 reported by the device probe, whereas the 4096-token set (528 MB) does not, so the small/medium shapes are largely L2-resident across the 100 replayed invocations. Consequence: pipeline ratios and effective rates from sub-L2 shapes must not be used to size an HBM Roofline or to choose a tile for the 4096-token regime.

findings.label: 64-token kernel is vector-bound but accounts for only 7.5% of eval latency; its 0.979 speedup is a host-plateau artifact
findings.backend_detail: msprof op_summary.csv for the 64x8x7168 bf16 workload; grid is (4,7)=28 blocks with BLOCK_M=16, BLOCK_N=1024.

evidence.metric: Task Duration(us) vs Task Wait Time(us) (rows 3-6)

findings.inference: At 64 tokens the vector pipeline is the busiest resource (0.797, 4.89 us) because bf16->fp32 conversion plus eight accumulations dominate once the 8.26 MB working set is L2-resident, while MTE2 is only 2.18 us. This kernel could plausibly be tightened, but it is 7.5% of the 98.11 us eval latency and the device waits 123-139 us for each launch, so no kernel change on this shape can recover the 2 us by which the candidate (98.11 us) trails the reference (96.06 us). The sub-1.0 speedup is therefore a host-cadence effect at the plateau, not a kernel deficit.

performance_interpretation: The five timing workloads split into two regimes. (A) 1/8/64/512 tokens: kernel duration is 2.57/4.32/7.38/35.75 us but eval latency is flat at 96.29/91.97/98.11/93.08 us - a 13.9x span in kernel time produces no eval-latency movement, and per-invocation Task Wait Time (device idle before the next launch) is 100-138 us for 1/8/64 tokens and 77-79 us at 512 tokens. These four are launch/host-cadence bound, with the kernel contributing 2.7%-38.4% of eval latency, so their speedups (1.05/1.11/0.98/2.72) are governed by the host floor rather than by kernel quality; the 2.72x at 512 tokens comes from the reference's much slower kernel (253 us), not from candidate kernel work. The round-1 change did lower this floor: round-1 latencies for the three smallest shapes were 131.01/127.77/125.73 us versus 96.29/91.97/98.11 us now, consistent with the plan's claim that dropping 6 runtime arguments and the mask path cut per-call host cost. (B) 4096 tokens: kernel 460.08 us accounts for 99.0% of the 464.77 us eval latency, Task Wait Time is 0.000-0.221 us (device continuously busy), and input+output traffic is 528.5 MB, giving ~1149 GB/s combined / ~1275 GB/s read-only while MTE2 is active. The plan's hypothesis is therefore confirmed for the host-cost mechanism and substantially confirmed for the large shape (1438.84->464.77 us, 379->~1149 GB/s, ~97% of the plan's own 1190 GB/s target), but 'saturates HBM' is NOT established: MTE2 is active only 80.4% of the kernel and the vendor op-profiler states 'MTE2 bandwidth utilization lower than 80% when active', so ~20% of the kernel has the load pipeline idle while the device is otherwise fully occupied.

next_experiment.action_description: For the >512-token path only, raise num_stages from 2 to 3 in _make_config (config line 60 of .kernelgen/evals/round-0002/main.py), keeping BLOCK_M=16, BLOCK_N=1024, num_warps=4, the EVEN specialization, the 3-runtime-argument signature and the <=512-token num_stages=1 branch exactly as they are. This adds one more in-flight 16x1024 bf16 row tile (32 KB) so the next k-slice load overlaps the current bf16->fp32 convert and accumulate, targeting the 19.6% of the 460 us kernel in which MTE2 is idle while every core is otherwise occupied.
next_experiment.expected_impact: If the residual MTE2 idleness is dependency exposure, kernel time falls from 460 us toward the ~368-400 us MTE2/overlap bound, so sglang_moe_sum_reduce-00004-timing eval latency moves from 0.4648 ms to roughly 0.405-0.425 ms, speedup rises from 5.18x to ~5.6-5.9x, and headline geo_mean rises from 1.7423 to ~1.78 (+2-3%). Conversely, if latency stays at ~460 us, the shape is effectively at its practical streaming roof (~1.15 TB/s) and this direction should be closed.
next_experiment.risks_and_rollback: UB budget is the real risk: 64 KB fp32 accumulator + 3 x 32 KB bf16 stage buffers is ~160 KB of the 192 KB UB, so stage 3 may fail to compile or cause spills that make the kernel slower. num_stages changes neither masks nor divisibility and touches no correctness semantics, so revert is a one-token config change back to 2 with no rollback risk to accuracy. If stage 3 will not compile or regresses, the documented fallback is BLOCK_M=8, BLOCK_N=1024, num_stages=3, which halves the accumulator to 32 KB and each stage buffer to 16 KB (grid becomes 512x7=3584 blocks); do not attempt BLOCK_N=3584 with BLOCK_M>=8, as the fp32 accumulator alone would exceed UB.
success_criteria: Full eval correctness PASSED on all three correctness workloads with matched_ratio 1.0 under the existing rtol/atol 0.015 contract.
sglang_moe_sum_reduce-00004-timing eval latency strictly below 0.4648 ms (profiler-observed mte2_ratio above 0.804 confirms the intended mechanism).
No regression on the host-bound plateau: 00000/00001/00002/00003 eval latencies stay within ~3 us of 96.29/91.97/98.11/93.08 us, since those shapes use the untouched num_stages=1 branch.
If 00004 latency improves by less than 2%, reject the change and record 00004 as bandwidth-limited at ~1.15 TB/s rather than retrying deeper pipelining.

warnings: msprof and simulator timing is diagnostic and is not eval latency; all speedup, candidate and reference latency figures come from get_profile_context.

The 'instruction' level is declared in service capabilities but did not complete for 00004: error 'profiling deadline expired during Ascend simulator kernel 0'. Partial artifacts (device OpProf metrics, 6 stages, detailed_kernel_count 1) were retained; the failure is not a kernel or device fault.
Pipeline ratios are per-core activity fractions and overlap in time; mte2 0.804 + vec 0.455 does not sum to a time decomposition and is not a bandwidth-utilization percentage.
The 00000 summary average kernel time (2.566 us) matches its steady-state rows (2.48-2.64 us); the first ~5 invocations are warm-up (4.9-6.9 us) and must not be used as the steady-state value.
Per-workload axes reported by get_profile_context are empty; shapes in profiled_workloads.axes were taken from .kernelgen/evals/round-0002/workloads.json.
open_questions: Instruction-level localization was not obtained: the 'instruction' profile for 00004 failed with 'profiling deadline expired during Ascend simulator kernel 0' (timeout.log, profile_id 71a07ab8afc44a489c9b87c61ecbb01e). The device OpProf stage of that same run did complete and produced the MTE2<80% conclusion, but no SASS/AscendC listing or PC-to-source mapping exists, so the claim that the 20% idle is load->use dependency exposure is inference from pipeline ratio plus the vendor's bandwidth verdict, not instruction-level proof.

No validated HBM peak for Ascend910B4-1 is available in the service context, so no quantitative Roofline is claimed. The measured ~1.15 TB/s combined (~1.28 TB/s read while MTE2 is active) is a derived rate, not a percentage of a verified ceiling; confirming or refuting headroom requires either a validated peak or the num_stages=3 result.

Whether the ~92-98 us small-shape floor is mostly harness-side (shared with the reference, hence not addressable) or candidate-side Python/launch cost remains unresolved; nothing in the profiler separates host API time from the measurement loop, and the HostToDevice entries in the execution trace are ph='f' flow arrows with no duration.

L2 residency for the sub-528 MB shapes is inferred from effective rate versus the probe's 176 MB L2 and was not verified with an L2 hit-rate counter (the detailed metrics were saved but only inside msprof-op-report.tar.gz, which this analysis could not extract).
